gaps.explanation: 'Valuable' means worth a lot of money; 'valued' means appreciated; 'invaluable' already means priceless, so it is not graded.

gaps.sentence: Take my ___ and sell the car before the prices fall.
gaps.explanation: 'Take my advice' — the noun form follows the possessive.

gaps.sentence: Factory workers are paid ___ at the end of each week.
gaps.hint: pay for manual work, usually weekly
gaps.explanation: 'Wages' are paid weekly, often in cash, for manual or unskilled work; salaries are monthly.

gaps.sentence: Should any dispute ___, the matter will go to arbitration.
gaps.explanation: 'Arise' = (problems, disputes) occur; 'rise' means go up and 'raise' needs an object.

gaps.sentence: There was ___ anything left in the fridge.
gaps.hint: adverb meaning almost not at all
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly' means almost not ('hardly anything'); 'hard' means with effort or solid.

gaps.sentence: Studying abroad is a wonderful ___ to practise your Spanish.
gaps.hint: a situation that lets you do something; pattern: ___ to do
gaps.explanation: 'Opportunity to do something' means a chance a situation gives you; 'possibility' is not followed by 'to'.

gaps.sentence: He ___ all knowledge of the missing file.
gaps.explanation: 'Deny all knowledge of something' is the fixed phrase.

gaps.sentence: One of the screws on the bracket has come ___.
